title: Matepe (thumb piano)
summary: The matepe is a lamellophone of Zimbabwe related to the mbira, with iron keys on stepped tiers of a board that sits inside a big gourd, the board ringed with shells that rattle with every note. The fingers weave a pattern that repeats round and round.
howToPlay: Every key is lit in order of pitch; the tip of each key is where the thumb plucks.
Notes fall toward a tip; strike it as the note lands. The key flexes and glows.
Start with the first cycle, then the answering one.
rules: A stroke on the pulse is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: The gourd makes the keys sound large and warm, and the shells add a bright rattle that is part of the sound.
credits: Tradition: the matepe; cycles written for this game
